facts.text: Hamilton City sprang to life in 1905 when a massive sugar beet plant opened, founded by James Hamilton and the Alta California Sugar Beet Company.
The towering silos of the former Holly Sugar Plant, once served by the California Northern Railroad, dominate the skyline and are visible from everywhere.
Hamilton City sits 151 feet above sea level, just 9.5 miles east of Orland and 10 miles west of Chico, right on the Sacramento River at mile 199.
The town’s first post office opened in 1906, marking the beginning of formal communication for the growing community.
Hamilton City’s roots trace back to a sugar beet processing plant that later became the Holly Sugar Plant, now owned by Nutrien after a 2021 renovation.
The community lies along the Sacramento River near mile marker 199, a detail that locals often use to describe their town’s location.
